text:
Maya Chen: customer reports intermittent 403s mid-stream right after token rotate. Happening ~1-2x/hour, only on streaming endpoints. Request ID from sample: r-19f8c2a7.
Kevin Lopez: can you paste the raw curl you used or exact headers? most of these are auth window issues.
Maya Chen: here's what they ran (redacted token) — they also hit through a corporate proxy.
```
curl -v \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: r-19f8c2a7" \n  -H "User-Agent: AcmeStreamer/1.2.3" \n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-4o-mini"
```
Olivia Gupta: quick check — are they rotating tokens client-side? If the client swaps the token while the socket is open we see auth windows cause a 403. Also proxy TLS session reuse can break with cookie/token combos.
support-bot: Attached server logs for r-19f8c2a7: "403 during auth refresh, upstream returned 401, fallback disabled" (log snippet available).
Maya Chen: they said token is rotated by a refresh endpoint; timeline looks like: token A in use, refresh->token B, stream continues with A for a bit then 403. Customer says the token TTL is 5m.
Kevin Lopez: ask them to collect a minimal curl reproduction that keeps the same headers and simulates mid-stream rotation. Also need tcpdump/pcap showing the TLS connection around the 403 and the client-side timeline. Provide exact commands: 
```
# tcpdump (linux)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/stream-traffic.pcap host api.redwood.com and port 443
# curl trace for headers/body
curl -v --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-19f8c2a7" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-4o-mini"
```
Olivia Gupta: ask them to keep the original socket open and then perform the token swap at the client, record timestamps for each step, and capture the exact error frame from the SSE stream.
Maya Chen: i already asked for pcap + curl trace; they uploaded a small bundle but redacted tokens. I need instructions for what to redact before they share privately.
Kevin Lopez: request they redact only the Authorization header value, but keep X-Request-ID and any trace IDs. Also include full response headers (we need Set-Cookie, WWW-Authenticate, any upstream 502/401). Ask them to annotate which TLS session IDs map to which timeline points.
Olivia Gupta: if proxy is in middle, ask for proxy logs (CONNECT timing) and whether proxy is doing TLS termination or passthrough. If termination, cert reuse can invalidate sessions.
Infra Debug: hypothesize: client rotates token but reuses same TCP/TLS session; token refresh endpoint may rotate claims server-side invalidating old token mid-connection causing short 403 window. Also some proxies rewrite Authorization headers on reconnect.
Maya Chen: customer requested a minimal one-shot curl that demonstrates the exact error so they can share with their infra team. Any suggestions to make it deterministic?
Kevin Lopez: suggest two-step reproducer: (1) open SSE stream with token A and log connection time; (2) call token refresh endpoint to get token B; (3) reuse same connection (no reconnect) and observe behaviour; if that triggers 403, we have a timing/auth-window issue. Provide a script template they can run locally.
```
# pseudocode for local repro (bash)
TOKEN_A=...
TOKEN_B=... # obtained by refresh call
# open stream in background
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_A" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-4o-mini" > /tmp/stream_out.txt &
STREAM_PID=$!
# wait 10s then rotate token (simulate client refresh)
sleep 10
# hit an endpoint to simulate refresh (real flow)
curl -s -X POST -d "..." https://auth.acme/refresh -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_A"
# keep stream running, check for 403s in /tmp/stream_out.txt
ps -p $STREAM_PID || echo "stream closed"
```
Maya Chen: i've sent a secure upload link and asked them to include the pcap + trace + a small annotated timeline file. Also asked to indicate their OS, curl version, and whether a proxy is used.
Olivia Gupta: once they upload, we should grep logs for r-19f8c2a7 and correlate the server-side auth cache eviction time. If it's a TTL mismatch we'll suggest sticky token strategy or server-side grace window.
Kevin Lopez: also ask customer to try forcing a reconnect after refresh as a short-term mitigation: close & re-open socket on token rotate. If that avoids 403, it's likely token-in-session invalidation.
Maya Chen: thanks — i'll follow up when bundle arrives. :thumbsup:
